name: Cameo Pink
lede: Cameo Pink is a light purplish pink from Ridgway's 1912 plates, so rare in our painting archive that it covers five per cent of the canvas in only one work.

sections.title: Two plates, two dates
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature plates it at plate XXVI, hue 71', tone f, hex #EFBBCC, though Ridgway's own printed swatch reads slightly differently, as #EEC8CD [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary cites that same 1912 plate at column C, chip 2 [1]. The library also carries a second Maerz and Paul citation dated 1925, plate 42, column G, chip 1; the two dictionaries disagree on which plate is the name's origin [1]. The ISCC-NBS committee's 1955 match places the color in block 253 among the "grayish purplish pink" names, 4.1 units away [1]. Its Munsell renotation is 4.7RP 8.0/5.4 [1].

Two library names sit at the same distance, 2.8 units: [[orchid-pink|Orchid pink]] and [[rosolane-pink|Rosolane Pink]], which are themselves the same hex as each other [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within six units of Cameo Pink covers at least five per cent of the canvas in only one of 23,781 paintings, Isaac Grünewald's 1917 *View of Stockholm*, where it covers 22 per cent of the canvas [2]. That makes it the rarest named color, and one of the rarest in the whole archive. These are photographs of varnished paintings, read as screen colors; a single match is not evidence of a pattern [2].
